summary: An Indologist, Leopold von Schroeder studied at Tartu/Dorpat under Leo Meyer, Leipzig, Jena, and under Rudolf von Roth. He held posts at the University of Tartu (~1877–1894), University of Innsbruck (~1896–1899), and University of Vienna as Professor (~1899–1920).

Leslie S. Kawamura worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He completed his PhD at the University of Saskatchewan under Herbert V. Guenther (~1971–1975) and served as a professor at the University of Calgary (~1976–2010).

Levi McLaughlin works in religious studies, Japanology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Tokyo and Princeton University under Jacqueline I. Stone. His posts include Kokugakuin University (2002–2004) and North Carolina State University as associate professor (2012).

Lewis Doney is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned an MA under Ulrich Pagel and a PhD at SOAS University of London, later holding posts at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (attested 2018) and University of Bonn (attested 2021).

Lewis Lancaster is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under Richard Hugh Robinson (~1963–1968). He held posts at the University of California, Berkeley from around 1967 to 2002, serving as Professor and Professor Emeritus.

Lhagpa Phuntshogs is a Tibetologist. He served as president of the Tibet Academy of Social Sciences (1983–1991), secretary-general of the Research Association for the Qinghai-Tibet Plateau (1991–2000), and became Director General of the China Tibetology Research Center in 2000.
Liang Cai works in Sinology and history and archaeology. She studied under Daniel Boucher and held a post as a junior scholar at the University of Arkansas (attested 2014).
Lili Zheng works in Buddhist studies. She earned a Master of Arts at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2011).

Lilla Russell-Smith specializes in history and archaeology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. She studied under Anna Eörsi and Pál Miklós, and completed a PhD at SOAS University of London.
Lin Heng is an Indology scholar who completed an MA at Silpakorn University under the supervision of Chainarong Klinnoi (attested 2015).
Linda Jean LaMacchia works in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. She earned her PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison under the supervision of David M. Knipe (attested 2001).
Linda Learman is a scholar in religious studies and Buddhist studies. She studied under doctoral supervisor Robert P. Weller and postdoctoral mentor Peter N. Gregory (attested 2005).
Linda Penkower specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at Columbia University in 1993 and served as a research fellow at Taisho University (attested 1983).
Lindsay G. McCune is a scholar in Tibetology and religious studies. She studied under teachers Kathleen M. Erndl and John Corrigan, and completed an MA supervised by Bryan J. Cuevas (attested 2007).
Ling Ji is a Sinologist who earned a PhD at the National University of Singapore under the supervision of Yuet Keung Lo (attested 2014).

Lionel David Barnett was an Indologist who studied at the University of Liverpool and Trinity College, Cambridge. He served at the British Museum (~1899–1936), University College London (~1906–1917), and SOAS University of London (~1917–1948).

Lionel Obadia works in religious and Buddhist studies. After completing a PhD at Lille University of Science and Technology (1997), he held posts at INALCO, KU Leuven, EPHE, Lille 3 University, and Lumière University Lyon 2 as Professor.

Liqian Liu was a scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He held posts at West China Union University (~1946–1949), the Ethnic Publishing House, and the translation administration department of the State Council of the People's Republic of China.

Lisa Grumbach specializes in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Japanology. She held an affiliation at Stanford University (attested 1996) and served as an assistant professor at the Institute of Buddhist Studies.
Lisa N. Owen specializes in history, archaeology, and Indology. She studied under Walter M. Spink and completed her PhD at the University of Texas at Austin under the supervision of Janice Leoshko.
